rationale: Tests understanding of which of Koch's postulates establishes causality, after the historical milestones block introduces all four postulates in sequence.
Consolidates the four ecological roles of microorganisms (commensal, mutualist, opportunist, pathogen) as related prompt–answer pairs after the roles table completes this learning point.
Tests visual recognition of bacterial morphology and arrangement — an inherently visual learning point — after the classification block introduces shapes and grouping patterns.
Tests classification of an organism into the correct microbial category using clinical clues, after the viruses/fungi/parasites block completes the full classification framework.
Tests precise recall of the four key definitions (sterilisation, disinfection, antisepsis, decontamination) that prevent dangerous clinical errors, as emphasised in the definitions block.
Tests understanding of standard autoclave parameters — the most widely used physical sterilisation method — after the physical methods block details conditions, applications, and quality control.
Tests the ability to select the correct sterilisation method for heat-labile instruments — a direct MI1.13 competency — after the chemical methods block introduces alternatives to heat sterilisation.
Tests the Spaulding-based clinical decision framework using a real-world sporicidal decontamination scenario, after the decision framework block completes the method-selection learning point.

Tests a common mechanistic misconception about crystal violet retention — impermeability versus dehydration-induced trapping — after the Gram stain principle block explains the CV-I complex and decolourisation.
Tests recall of the correct sequence of Gram staining steps — a practical procedure MBBS students must perform — after the procedure block details each step.

Tests systematic interpretation of a Gram stain in a clinical scenario — applying morphology and Gram reaction to organism identification — after the interpretation block presents the reporting framework.
Tests understanding of the ZN staining principle — specifically why mycobacteria are acid-fast — after the ZN principle and procedure block explains the role of mycolic acid.

Tests the ability to identify a parasite from stool microscopy findings combined with clinical presentation, after the routine stool examination block describes specimen processing and microscopic identification.
